_comment: What this repo puts in the chuk-datasets catalog (chuk-datasets.fly.dev).
CI runs `register.py verify` against this file on every push: it recomputes
each content_sha from the files on disk and fails the build if the catalog
does not carry a version with that sha. That closes the loop between the
corpus CI measures against and the corpus the catalog claims was measured.
Classes are the spec's enum (§103): pretrain-stream | eval-set |
probe-corpus | midtrain-corpus | raw-source. None of these are training
data, so all three are raw-source; the envelope carries the real format.
To add a dataset: add an entry, run `register.py register datasets.json`
with a write-scoped CHUK_DATASETS_API_KEY, then commit.

datasets.name: v11/corpus
datasets.description: v11 tokenizer benchmark/spot-check corpus: prose + code across 7 languages, 32 files.

provenance.note: Hand-assembled. This is the corpus the byte-safety round-trip gate runs against (bench/tokenizer_bench.py roundtrip): 0 UNK, 32/32 files pass as of the 2026-07-24 fix. If this corpus changes, that gate result no longer describes what the catalog holds -- hence CI verification.

datasets.name: v11/wordnet-lemmas
datasets.description: WordNet lemmas filtered by word frequency (min Zipf 2.5): 27,796 kept of 77,174 raw. A knowledge source the v11 vocabulary is assembled from.

provenance.note: Provenance fields above are read from the file's own header, not asserted here. WordNet carries the Princeton WordNet licence; this extraction is lemma strings plus frequencies.

datasets.name: v11/tokenizer
datasets.description: The published v11 tokenizer build: HF tokenizer.json + configs, the knowledge vocabulary listing, and the native Rust vocab binary. 71,260 pieces, byte-safe.

published_to.note: Package versions deliberately not recorded here. This dataset IS the vocabulary; the crates and wheel are code that reads it, and they version independently -- pinning a version string in this entry would go stale every release without the dataset having changed. The tokenizer.json sha256 below is the identity.

provenance.note: tokenizer.json sha256 10dd51100331ab503115db23eee7e8dc3e360e3aed697c8a2e1b12b8f46031ae, byte-identical to the HF Hub copy. Separately, the `tokenizer_sha` recorded on tiny-model/v11-rust-tokenized-* versions (873f44dea58558abd355454b6a22281ba69ad5afe850d05e48c271536471905b) is the plain file sha of v11.vocab.bin, which is a member of THIS dataset -- that is how those token streams tie back to a cataloged tokenizer.
